# Results — Study 746 (HQ-Relocation)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The question — **"is a
headquarters-relocation announcement (tax/incentive driven) a signal, or a distraction?"** —
tested as a textbook short-window **event study**: around each dated HQ-move announcement, the
**cumulative abnormal return** (CAR) is the stock's return minus a **market-model** fit
(`stock = α + β·SPY`) estimated on a clean pre-event window, cumulated over the event window. A
tidy relocation database is not freely available, so events come from a **hardcoded, labelled
table** of ~20 documented HQ moves, 2010-2025 (tax/incentive vs other rationale). Offline core +
synthetic control are deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — each event ticker + SPY (public, no key) |
| Event table | hardcoded `HQ_MOVES` (ticker, announce date, tax/other), fingerprint **3fdda93c2d9a** |
| As-of | 2026-06-30 |
| Events in table | **20**, all with usable pre-event price history (long-listed large caps) |
| Buckets | **14 tax/incentive** / **6 other** rationale |
| Benchmark / model | market model `stock = α + β·SPY`, 120-day estimation window, 10-day gap |
| Event window | CAR **[0, +2]** trading days (canonical); robustness over [0,0], [−1,+1], [0,+4] |
| Drift leg | post-announcement **[+1, +63]** (~one quarter), entered the day after the headline |
| Entry / costs | tradable drift variant enters **+1 day**; one-way 10-bps round-trip |

> **Two named caveats (on the Signal axis).** (1) The **tax/other label** is the believers'
> own framing and is subjective at the margin — a Texas move cuts *both* state tax and
> cost-of-living, and GE's Boston move came with $145M of state incentives yet was sold as a
> talent play. (2) The table is **selected on salience** (the moves famous enough to be
> remembered and dated) and every name **survived** to keep trading — a mild survivorship tilt,
> and several vivid moves are un-priceable around the event (Burger King's pre-IPO Canada
> inversion, Mylan→Netherlands, Walgreens' *abandoned* Swiss inversion). Neither moves the
> verdict: it rests on the *sample size* and on the *absence of any move at all*, both robust.

## The signal — abnormal return around the announcement (canonical CAR[0,+2])

| bucket | n | mean CAR | win-rate (CAR>0) | *t* vs 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **tax / incentive** | 14 | **+0.45%** | 50% | **+0.35** |
| **other rationale** | 6 | **−0.40%** | 67% | **−0.35** |
| all events | 20 | +0.20% | 55% | +0.21 |

**tax − other = +0.85pp**, Welch ***t* = +0.50**, all-events placebo ***p* = 0.735** (share of
random same-size non-event windows on the same names whose mean CAR matches/beats the real set).
Read it carefully: there is **nothing here**. The announcement CAR is a fifth of a percent, a
coin-flip win-rate, and a *t* an order of magnitude short of significance; splitting by *why* the
company moved changes nothing (the gap is +0.85pp at *t* = 0.50). The market greets an HQ move
with a shrug.

## Not even an announcement-*day* jolt (window [0,0])

| window | what it measures | all mean | *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **[0, 0]** | the announcement-*day* repricing | **+0.18%** | **+0.23** | 55% | 0.588 |
| [0, +2] | a holdable 3-day window | +0.20% | +0.21 | 55% | 0.735 |

Unlike a forced-CEO ouster (which *does* jolt the tape on the day), an HQ-move announcement does
**not** even move the stock on the announcement day: **+0.18%** at *t* = 0.23, placebo *p* = 0.59.
There is no instantaneous repricing to find, tradable or not.

## The drift the "signal" camp needs — a whiff, but inside the noise

Enter the day after the headline and hold; the "signal" camp says the tax saving gets priced in
over the following weeks.

| drift window | all mean | *t* | tax mean | tax *t* | placebo *p* | net @10bps |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [+1, +21] (~1 month) | −0.06% | −0.03 | +0.85% | +0.26 | — | −0.16% |
| **[+1, +63] (~1 quarter)** | **+3.39%** | **+1.34** | +4.66% | +1.46 | **0.301** | +3.29% |

Over a quarter the CAR drifts **+3.4%** (tax bucket +4.7%) — the one number that leans the
"signal" way. But it is **not significant** (*t* = 1.34, placebo *p* = 0.30: a random quarter on
these names looks this good 30% of the time), it appears only at the longest horizon, and on a
20-name survivor tape it is exactly what a couple of big Texas movers riding a bull market look
like. It fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar, and the one-month leg is flat. There is no drift you could
certify.

## Robustness — flat in every window choice

| event window | all mean | *t* | tax − other | diff *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| [0, 0] | +0.18% | +0.23 | −0.49pp | −0.41 |
| **[0, +2]** (canonical) | +0.20% | +0.21 | +0.85pp | +0.50 |
| [−1, +1] | +1.10% | +0.88 | +0.23pp | +0.12 |
| [0, +4] | +0.34% | +0.32 | +1.86pp | +0.97 |

No window crosses *t* = 1, let alone *t* = 2, and the tax−other gap never gets near significance.
The non-result does not hinge on the window.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, small samples are weak

A deterministic per-event abnormal-return panel (14 tax / 12 other) with a **plantable
tax-bucket CAR edge**:

| planted tax edge | tax mean | tax *t* | other mean | tax−other *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0 bps** (no edge) | −0.43% | −0.49 | −1.10% | **+0.45** |
| **+500 bps** (large) | +4.57% | +5.12 | −1.10% | **+3.79** |

With **no** planted edge the tax−other test stays comfortably below *t* = 2 (it cannot fake
significance from ~a dozen events per bucket). Only an **implausibly large** +5%/event planted
edge drives the difference to *t* = 3.8. The control proves both things at once: the measurement
engine recovers a real effect when one exists, **and** a couple-dozen events is far too small to
detect any HQ-relocation edge of plausible size. That is the whole lesson.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The announcement CAR is **+0.20% at *t* = 0.21** (placebo *p* = 0.74); even
  the announcement *day* is **+0.18% at *t* = 0.23**; the tax−other gap is **+0.85pp at *t* =
  0.50**; and the only positive lean — a **+3.4% quarter drift** — sits at ***t* = 1.34**
  (placebo *p* = 0.30), short of the bar. Nothing here clears *t* = 1. The tax/other label is
  subjective and the tape is salience-selected — both named on this axis. Indistinguishable from
  noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no announcement-day move to capture and no significant
  post-announcement drift; the one whiff (+3.4% over a quarter, *t* = 1.34) is un-certifiable and
  is what a handful of big-cap Texas movers in a bull market produce by construction. No
  NAV-scale, sign-stable edge at any horizon.
- **Signal or distraction? — NON-EVENT.** The folklore's two camps — "the market prices the tax
  saving" (buy) and "an address change is theatre hiding a weak business" (fade) — are **both
  unsupported**. There is no significant positive pop (no signal) and no significant negative
  drift (no distraction penalty). On the tape, announcing a new headquarters is, on average, a
  non-event.
